survey: A saloon swing-door set. Two dark wooden posts stand upright on square base blocks that sit flat on the plank floor, and the floor shadow shows they make contact. A horizontal lintel beam rests on top of both posts and overhangs them slightly. Two light-wood half-doors hang at mid-height between the posts, as real saloon doors do. Each door is hung from its own post by two gold hinges, one near the top and one near the bottom, on the post's front face. Both doors have a matching build: outer frame, five vertical spindles, a middle rail and a solid lower panel, with a slightly dished top rail. The doors meet in the middle with a small gap, both facing the camera at three-quarter view. The left door is swung very slightly toward the viewer.

errors.where: Left door, its right edge and bottom rail
errors.what: The left door is slightly skewed against the right door. Its thick right edge and down-sloping bottom rail suggest it is swung open, yet its two hinges stay flat against the post face as if it were closed. The two leaves don't quite read as mirrored doors hanging in one plane.

fix: Make both saloon door leaves mirror images, hanging closed in the same plane between the posts, with level, parallel bottom rails. Each door hangs from its post by two hinges sitting at the door's edge.
